newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - VIVUS says FDA issues dealt with.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - VIVUS says FDA issues dealt with.

text.p: Vivus Inc Chief Financial Officer David Yntema said the company corrected the deficiencies raised by the Food and Drug Administration during a recent inspection and sees no long-term impact on shipments.
He added that he saw the sharp drop in Vivus shares on Monday as "a potential overreaction" to its announcement that shipments had been slowed because of the FDA review.
"During the review, we had to divert resources we normally devote to final testing and releasing of the products and we weren't able to release as much as previously," he said.

Vivus, whose stock has been extremely volatile since the FDA approved its treatment for male impotence at the beginning of the year, declined to disclose the issues raised by the FDA in its first post-approval inspection of its manufacturing facility. But Yntema said the company had been able to correct or develop action plans to correct all the issues cited.
Despite the delay in shipments, the company has not lost any production, only stockpiled some of it. He said all the stockpiled inventories should be shipped by the end of April.
Vivus shares were down 8-1/8 to 40 on Monday and have fallen from a peak of 81-1/4, reached shortly after its impotence treatment was approved.
